newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daido Hoxan mulls taking over Tateho Chem - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daido Hoxan mulls taking over Tateho Chem - paper.

text.p: Daido Hoxan Corp is considering taking over troubled Tateho Chemical Industries Co Ltd, a business daily reported on Friday.

Daido Hoxan is in talks with Sakura Bank, through which Tateho Chemical does most of its financial transactions, concerning the elimination of some of Tateho Chemical's debts before it takes over the firm, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
A spokesman for Daido Hoxan was not immediately available for comment on the report.
Tateho Chemical said on Monday that on a group basis the company's liabilities appeared to have exceeded its assets by about 1.4 billion yen in the financial year that ended on March 31.
Tateho also said its U.S. subsidiary's liabilities exceeded its assets by 256 million yen at the end of March 1996, but added that the U.S. subsidiary moved into the black during fiscal 1996/97.

The paper said one of the firms that merged to form Daido Hoxan took a stake in Tateho Chemical in 1988 to help it out of difficulties. When Daido Hoxan was formed in 1993, it began discussing a takeover of Tateho Chemical with Sakura Bank.
The recent dismissal of Daido Hoxan president Shigeru Mizushima, who was against a takeover, gives more leverage to chairman Hiroshi Aoki, who is in favour of it, the paper said.
